## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical equipment problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running without hydraulic load, indicating a mechanical failure or disconnection. Although routine maintenance was performed and most components remain in good condition, the pump failure prevents normal system operation and poses a risk of motor damage from overheating.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) measures 11 inches in a 48-inch tank, placing the system well within normal operating parameters. No pumping is indicated at this time based on solids content alone.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good | Baffles intact; no visible structural damage |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Cleaned and reseated during this visit; light soiling observed |
| Effluent Pump (0.5 hp, 115V) | CRITICAL | See Pump Status below |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals observed |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no ponding or breakout observed |
| Liquid Level | At Outlet | Normal operating level |

## PUMP STATUS -- CRITICAL
The effluent pump measured 1.6 amps during operation against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This represents 22.2% of full load amperage. A pump running at this load level is operating without meaningful hydraulic resistance, indicating one or more of the following:

- The pump impeller is broken or missing
- The discharge line is severed, disconnected, or blocked at the pump outlet
- The pump is running dry (no fluid present in the pump housing)

**Any of these conditions will cause rapid motor overheating and failure.** The pump must be inspected and repaired or replaced immediately. Do not continue operating the system in this state.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (Critical Priority):**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. A qualified technician must inspect the pump for impeller damage, check the discharge line for disconnection or blockage, and verify that fluid is reaching the pump housing. Do not operate the system until the pump is repaired or replaced.

**Routine (Next Maintenance Visit):**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is restored to normal operation.
- Confirm pump amp draw returns to the 5.0-6.5 amp range during normal operation.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### The Pump Problem
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious condition that will damage the motor if left unaddressed. The pump motor relies on the cooling effect of pumping fluid; running dry or under no load causes rapid overheating. Have a service technician inspect the pump and discharge line immediately.

### Solids and Tank Health
Your tank solids are at a healthy level -- about 23 percent of tank volume. The scum layer is normal, and the sludge depth is well within range. The tank itself is in good condition. Once the pump is repaired, your system will return to normal operation.

### Dispersal Field
The dispersal field shows no signs of stress or saturation. Surface conditions are dry and normal.
